newsitem.title: UK: Israel Fund considers restructuring options.
newsitem.headline: Israel Fund considers restructuring options.

text.p: Investment trust Israel Fund Plc said on Monday it was considering restructuring into an open-ended offshore structure.
The company said in August it was reviewing options for enhancing shareholder value, principally looking to reduce its discount to net asset value on a long term basis.

It said the change would permit regular issues and redemption of shares, subject to certain restrictions, but it depended on a number of matters, including clearances from tax, regulatory and other authorities, the court, and shareholders.
A detailed review of restructuring options was continuing.

It also said it had inadvertently breached one of the conditions for investment trust status between September 1996 and March 1997 by maintaining holdings in a company and its subsidiaries which marginally exceeded 15 per cent.

"While the board expects that the breach will have the result that the company will not qualify as an investment trust for the accounting period commencing February 1, 1996, no additional tax is expected to be incurred," it said in a statement.
It said it was taking action to remedy the position.
Also, the accounting period ending January 31, 1997 will be extended to March 31, and it intends to be able to qualify for investment trust status for the new accounting period commencing April 1.
